aj: Quick perf note — after the prefill+decode unified batching change I ran the perf harness on 13B-4q and saw a weird tail regression on decode p95 (short seqs). prefill throughput improved but decode p95 is ~2.1x higher under low-token requests. Anyone else see this?

marta: Yup saw similar in canary. Looks like when prefill and decode mix in the same batch we get more context-switches and some KV cache churn. Short decodes are penalized.

kai: Do we have profiler traces (nvprof / nsight) for the problematic runs? suspect kernel selection is falling back to the generic attention kernel for decode because sequence lengths vary inside a mixed batch.

aj: I attached the flame summary from the harness run earlier: `prefill_decode_mixed_17106047.flame.svg` — high tail on kernels labeled `attn_generic` during token generation. Prefill kernels look fine.

infra-bot: deploybot: perf-check job #3245 finished — baseline: p95_decode=48ms, canary: p95_decode=101ms, prefill_throughput +14% :rocket:

marta: My hypothesis: mixing prefill (longer seqs, warm KV writes) with decode (shorter seqs, heavy KV reads) triggers kernel selector to choose a safer but slower attention path to support the longest sequence in batch. Also KV cache alignment causes extra memcpy on decode paths.

sophia: We already had a bucketed kernel selector but it used batch-level max-seqlen. Might need phase-aware selection: pick kernel per sub-batch or split batch by phase.

kai: Agreed. Two concrete levers: 1) separate prefill vs decode queues and form homogeneous micro-batches for kernel selection; 2) add a phase-aware fallback that prefers fast decode kernels when decode tokens dominate.

aj: I prototyped a queue policy change: keep two simultaneous queues, prefill_queue and decode_queue. Token budget assignment: prefill_budget=1024 tokens or 50% of tokens in-flight, decode_budget=256 tokens or 25% for low-latency. If decode queue has low occupancy but latency target missed, prioritize decode.

marta: Nice. Can you paste the config snippet?

aj: Sure. snippet:```yaml
batching:
  phase_aware: true
  queues:
    - name: prefill
      token_budget: 1024
      max_batch_items: 8
      prefer_kernel: compile_prefill
    - name: decode
      token_budget: 256
      max_batch_items: 16
      latency_target_ms: 40
      prefer_kernel: compile_decode
  dynamic_routing:
    decode_priority_threshold_ms: 20
    scale_down_prefill_when_decode_slow: true
```

kai: That looks reasonable. Couple of comments: token_budget numbers should be workload-driven (median prefill tokens from traffic). Also ensure kernel compilation artifacts exist for compile_decode for small seqlen fast path or you'll hit compile fallback time.

sophia: From tracing perspective we should add `phase_label` to span metadata so we can filter prefill vs decode perf. Also add KV cache miss metric per phase — I think cache misses spike when mixed.

marta: I ran an A/B with separate queues (local harness): results: decode p95 down ~30% for short seqs, overall throughput +12%, but there's a regression for mid-sized prefill batches where we ended up using the incorrect conv-attn kernel — +6% latency there. Need kernel selector tweak.

aj: Hmm kernel selector regression probably from our heuristic that picks kernel based on average seq length. When batching homogeneous prefill batches avg==max so fine, but when we split by phase we need selector to prefer throughput-optimized conv kernels for prefill (even if memory slightly higher).

kai: Propose weighting scheme: score = alpha*latency + beta*memory. For prefill alpha lower (we care throughput) and for decode alpha high (we care latency). Also add explicit kernel hints in phase config (prefer_kernel entry).

sophia: I built a tiny perf probe to vary alpha/beta and run microbench. For Llama2-chat-13B-4q, alpha=0.8/beta=0.2 for decode and alpha=0.4/beta=0.6 for prefill produced best tradeoffs. Will share numbers.

aj: Good. Two more notes: 1) KV cache warmup — add a small prefetch_kv flag at end of prefill that pre-allocates cache slices used by decode to avoid memcpy stalls. 2) batching latency budget enforcement: if decode latency_target_ms exceeded, we should flush decode microbatch even if token_budget not full.

marta: Agree. Also we saw a perf regression when prefetch_kv set too aggressively — it caused extra GPU memory churn on multi-tenant. Need to gate prefetch behind mem-availability check.

kai: I'll open a ticket to add kernel scoring by phase + mem guard for prefetch. aj can you log the A/B harness config and upload traces?

aj: Will do. Uploading harness config and flamegraphs to the perf bucket now: s3://redwood-perf/prefill-decode-phase/17106047/ — includes perf diff, nvprof snapshots, and the microbench.

sophia: Next steps from infra side: add phase tags to traces, export KV-cache-misses-per-phase, and modify the dashboard to show prefill vs decode p95 separately.

marta: I'll run long-run nightly with tuned alpha/beta and tuned token budgets (prefill_budget=900-1100, decode_budget=128-512 depending on traffic) and report results tomorrow.

aj: TL;DR: mixed batching caused kernel fallback + KV churn -> separate queues + phase-aware kernel scoring + token budget + prefetch gating reduces decode tail. Need to finish kernel selector changes and add telemetry. Assignments: kai->kernel selector ticket, sophia->tracing changes, marta->nightly runs, aj->upload traces + config.

infra-bot: ticketbot: created RED-1287 "phase-aware kernel scoring" assigned to kai

marta: cool, thanks. I'll post follow-up with numbers. :thumbsup:
